acceptance_criteria.notes: Policy, run-time ship_event, opt-in archiving, standing orders, five escalation kinds and cadence all exist and their tests pass on both engines (crew-core 212 tests: 145 passed, 0 failed, 67 skipped, interpreter and --bytecode --strict-bytecode). Brief item 5 lists six escalation triggers; 'a request no standing order covers' is not implemented and not declared as dropped. The compatibility promise (crew-sim loop reproduced exactly) holds to about 20 ticks only. K4 (3,650 turns in 2 s) is met only at yearly cadence and only with no escalation rules; the game's rule set stops the same skip at tick 0.

correctness_robustness.notes: Archiving drops by direct id/cause match only and keeps ev-/sf- evidence; completedCount is exact for Completed tasks (tallied at fold, live count added). Held/pending/bank/unresolved-relief protection is sound by reading but untested. Auto-captain order and ids match the old loop for consent/orders captains under 20 ticks. Resume after a refusal escalation at the same tick reuses request ids (defect 2). Stale-offer handling changes behaviour past tick 20 (defect 1).

test_quality.notes: auto_test covers refusal stop, breakdown once, trust floor, argument, major, weekly cadence and decode. Missing: breakdown/trust re-arm, resume after escalation, stale offers, partial last cadence block, pending-advance continuation, archive protection of pending/bank/relief/issue, archive under watch-v3, a mid-session ship_event, policy switch with pending requests refused.

docs_bookkeeping.notes: CHANGELOG, sprint plan and outcome are candid about K4 partial and the argument rarity (2/20). #1812 (second call site, 10.3 -> 24.6 GB) and #1814 (list tail copying, repro numbers) exist and say what the docs claim. Deductions: 'crew-sim output unchanged' and 'byte-identical' statements are false beyond 20 ticks and for the added escalations key; the missing sixth escalation rule is not mentioned; lab ailang.lock for crew_core was stale against the tree when run (warning 'content changed'); sprint JSON still in_progress (expected pre-landing).

defects.issue: The auto-captain does not reproduce the previous crew-sim loop past tick ~20: offers are agreed at tick+20, and auto treats an Offered task whose agreement is due as stale (not busy, not re-asked), where the old loop kept the worker busy and re-asked. I ran the pre-sprint crew_sim.ail/sim_cli.ail (6dfc0fa) against HEAD crew_core, processing-cascade, orders, seeds 1..3: 20 turns identical except the new 'escalations':{} key in every row; 40 turns differ (offers 32 vs 37, starts 27 vs 28, refusal_reasons unauthorized 95 vs 92); 80 turns consent also differ (consent_required 39 vs 0). Sprint JSON K3 note 'crew-sim output byte-identical through auto' and the outcome text are therefore true only for the 12-turn claims runs. The new behaviour is arguably better, but it is an undeclared change.
defects.suggestion: State it in the CHANGELOG and sprint outcome (stale offers lapse after the agreement's 20 ticks; crew_sim/1 rows gain 'escalations'), or gate it behind an Orders field to keep the old loop; add a test at 25+ turns.

defects.issue: A refusal_under_orders escalation stops before the advance, so tick is unchanged; the next advanceAuto call starts with first = tick+1 = the same turn number and re-issues request ids p<turn>-<task> and c<turn>-<task> that are already in the bank. Probe (orders, firstContact, refusal rule, 6 resumes of 40): at tick 3 the resumed call logs 'ask: {host: request capacity/id/clock}' for scientist, diplomat and medic. In check-ins that is a noisy error act; in persuade the failed ask gives label '' and decide() then calls begin() under start=always, i.e. an unescalated override of a worker who had not been heard (inferred from the code, not reproduced).
defects.suggestion: Derive the turn number from a counter in AutoState (or include a call counter / seq in ids), or make the refusal stop also advance a half-turn marker; add a resume-after-refusal test asserting zero error acts.

defects.issue: The brief's sixth escalation trigger, 'a request no standing order covers', is not implemented, and CHANGELOG/sprint do not say it was dropped. Orders have no 'uncovered request' notion (concern/defer replies are auto-handled).
defects.suggestion: Either implement a rule kind (e.g. 'uncovered', fired on a reply label outside the orders' vocabulary) or record the omission and its reason on #137.

defects.issue: Ship-event evidence text now includes a 'major' field when the event has one. Scheduled events with major set were valid in 0.2.0, so their evidence text, state and trace change; the 'recordings replay byte-identically' promise holds only because no parity fixture has a major event. The changelog mentions it as a feature, not as a state change. Needed so auto can detect majors by evidence text.
defects.suggestion: Say in the CHANGELOG that 0.2.0 scenarios with major events produce different evidence text, or keep the old text and detect majors from scenario.events by the new evidence id (ev-<id>).

defects.issue: held() blocks archiving of any task that has a conversation issue, including closed and answered ones, and issues/speech are never removed. In watch-v3 sessions (start accepts keep with watch-v3) tasks that were ever discussed are never archived and the conversation store grows without bound. No test runs archiving with watch-v3.
defects.suggestion: Only hold on open issues, and fold closed issues and their speech with the task, or reject keep for watch-v3 and document it; add a test.

defects.issue: K4 timing is honest about cadence but the 1.9 s figure is for a skip with no escalation rules. With the shipped escalation.json the same --skip 3650 stops at tick 0 on the first declined offer (refusal_under_orders). I measured (orders, processing-cascade, archive 30, no rules): yearly cadence 3.3 s wall including startup (decisions 50), monthly 29.6 s (610 decisions, 587 refusals). The monthly figure is below the doc's 'about 60 s weekly or monthly', plausible for weekly. The game will rarely complete a 10-year skip in one call.
defects.suggestion: State in the changelog that the speed figures are without rules and that rules stop the skip; report a --skip run with the escalation rules and the number of resumes.

defects.issue: Counting mode (decideTurn/finishTurn) records at most one escalation per rule per turn: breakdown and trust_floor pick head(first uncrossed worker) and argument/major pick head(new evidence). Two workers crossing, or two events, in the same turn count once, so escalations-per-year claims undercount slightly; two breakdown rules on the same indicator share the 'indicator/worker' raised key and interfere. Re-arming only runs in the no-new-crossing branch, and not at all for later rules after an earlier rule escalates in the same turn.
defects.suggestion: Fold over all crossing workers / all new evidence ids; key raised by rule index.

defects.issue: Run-time events are appended to s.scenario.events and their ev-/sf- evidence and per-crew knowledge are never archived (limits: evidence 2048, knowledge 8192, ~15 knowledge rows per event for 15 crew), so a long game raising many events will hit CapacityExceeded; scenario.events also grows without a cap and is re-scanned on each advance. decodeShipEvent at tick 0 (at forced to >=1, then overwritten with 0) works and is tested; mid-session events and the duplicate-id check against scenario.events are covered only for tick 0.
defects.suggestion: Add a documented ceiling and a test (e.g. 500 events), or archive ev-/sf- evidence beyond a window while keeping seen() true via a counter or id list.

defects.issue: Archiving truncates state.accepted to the newest 512, so an old operation id could be accepted again if a host replayed it; undocumented in the CHANGELOG beyond 'operation log keeps its newest 512'. Also protection of pending/bank/unresolved reliefs in held() is correct by reading but has no test.
defects.suggestion: Document the idempotency window and add tests for archive-skips-held cases.

defects.issue: At evaluation time both locks show as modified in the clone, and running the lab warns 'dependency sunholo/crew_core content changed (locked ... current ...)'. The committed lab lock does not match the committed crew_core tree.
defects.suggestion: Run ailang lock after the final crew_core edit and commit the result before the PR.

summary: PASS, 74/100. The additive surface (policy, ship_event, archive, auto, cadence) works, both engines pass, and the sprint is candid about K4 and the rare arguments. The promise 'crew-sim loop reproduced exactly' is only true to ~20 ticks (stale offers), the one-turn-resume after a refusal escalation reuses request ids, one of the six brief escalation triggers is missing without notice, and 0.2.0 scheduled major events change evidence text.
